issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) while the problem statement and the solution expect addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch in parameters will confuse students and prevent them from implementing or testing the method as specified (e.g., students implementing addGuestStudents(int) will not satisfy the template's method declaration and automated tests expecting the single-parameter variant).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's method signature match the specification and solution by changing the template declaration to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO */ } (or provide an overloaded single-parameter version). Alternatively, if the boolean parameter is intentional, update the problem statement and solution to document and use the two-parameter signature consistently.

issues.description: The template Lecture.addGuestStudents method signature includes an extra boolean parameter (addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput)) which does not match the problem statement UML and the solution implementation that specify addGuestStudents(int): void. This signature mismatch creates a mapping barrier: students are instructed to implement/use addGuestStudents(int) but the provided template stub requires a different method signature, leading to confusion and compile-time mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template method signature to match the UML and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). Alternatively provide an overload public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) that delegates to the boolean-parameter variant, and update the TODO/comment to reflect the expected signature.
